title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is very faint. It is a first draft of the definition that is rewritten more legibly on the next page, and what can be read agrees with that fair copy. Setting: A is a commutative Dedekind ring with fraction field K, and C is an A-préadditive category. The margin note explains the term: the Hom sets are A-modules and composition is bilinear, which is the same as an additive category together with a ring map A → End(id_C).

C is called a 'catégorie de Deuring (relative à A)' if condition (D) holds: there is an object X such that
(a) O = End(X) is a maximal A-order in End(X)⊗_A K, and this algebra is Azumaya (central simple) over K;
(b) for every right O-module P that is projective of rank 1 (meaning locally on Spec A isomorphic to O), the object P⊗_O X exists in C;
(c) the functor P ↦ P⊗_O X is an equivalence from rank-1 projective right O-modules onto C.

The page then begins the remark, completed on the next page, that if (D) holds for one object it holds for every object. In modern terms this is Morita theory for maximal orders: for an invertible O-module P, O' = End_O(P) is again a maximal order in the same central simple algebra, and Q ↦ Q⊗_{O'} P matches invertible O'-modules with invertible O-modules. The left-margin notes appear to discuss whether (a) is independent of (b) and (c).

Purpose: the previous page computes Weil numbers, p-adic units of Weil numbers and a group H/μ2, i.e. the motivic Galois group of the supersingular part. This page abstracts Deuring's theorem. With A = Z, supersingular elliptic curves over F̄_p with Hom groups as Z-modules form a category equivalent to invertible right modules over a maximal order O of the quaternion algebra B_{p,∞}; its isomorphism classes correspond to the left ideal classes of O. Grothendieck is axiomatizing this as an integral, Morita-theoretic structure to be used in a 'Galois theory of motives' over Z rather than over Q.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this faint draft. The next page fixes one ambiguity: 'projectif de rang 1' over a noncommutative O must mean locally on Spec A isomorphic to O, not rank 1 over A. For maximal orders, local projectives of the right K-rank are automatically locally isomorphic to O, so the notion is sound.
Condition (a) only asks that the generic fibre be Azumaya. In the Deuring case O itself is not Azumaya over Z: it ramifies at p. This is consistent with the definition but worth noting.

ideas.what: Axiomatic notion of a 'Deuring category' over a Dedekind ring A: an A-linear category equivalent to the invertible right modules over a maximal order in a central simple K-algebra, defined intrinsically by the existence of a generating object X.
ideas.modern_name: Category of invertible modules over a maximal order / Deuring correspondence in categorical form (cf. Kohel's thesis; Jordan–Keeton–Poonen–Rains–Shepherd-Barron–Tate on abelian varieties isogenous to E^n)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941) for supersingular curves vs ideal classes; categorical equivalence made explicit later (Kohel 1996; Jordan–Keeton–Poonen–Rains–Shepherd-Barron–Tate 2018)

ideas.what: Independence of the condition from the chosen object: the Morita equivalence between maximal orders O and End_O(P) for invertible P.
ideas.modern_name: Morita equivalence of maximal orders / Brandt groupoid of connecting ideals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Brandt, Deuring, Eichler; standard (Reiner, Maximal Orders)

ideas.what: A-préadditive category characterized as an additive category with a ring map A → End(id_C).
ideas.modern_name: A-linear category via the centre of the category

missed.claim: In the context of motivic Galois theory (1965), Grothendieck singles out integral 'Deuring categories', i.e. Z-linear categories of supersingular objects equivalent to invertible modules over a maximal quaternion order. This places Deuring's correspondence inside an integral, Morita-theoretic framework for motives with Z-coefficients, decades before the categorical Deuring equivalence was written down.
missed.quote: Une catégorie A-préadditive C est dite "catégorie de Deuring (relative à A)" si ... le foncteur P ↦ P⊗_O X est une équivalence
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early instance of thinking about integral (Z-linear) structure on categories of motives over finite fields. That theme is now active in work on integral motives and in isogeny-based cryptography, where the Deuring correspondence is central. Its significance is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics, Deuring's correspondence and Morita theory of maximal orders, is classical. The axiomatic name and its use for integral motives in 1965 are a modest unpublished historical detail, and the page itself is only a faint draft of the next page.
transcription_corrections: 'catégorie de Dedekind' should read 'catégorie de Deuring (relative à A)'.
'Une catégorie ... C' should read 'Une catégorie A-préadditive C'.
Condition '0)' is '(D)'; a) reads 'L'anneau O = End(X) est un ordre maximal de End(X)⊗_A K, qui est une algèbre d'Azumaya sur K'.
b) reads 'Pour tout module projectif (de rang 1) P sur O, P⊗_O X existe comme objet de C'; c) reads 'Le foncteur P ↦ P⊗_O X est une équivalence de catégories...'.
The line after c) begins 'Si cette condition est vérifiée pour un objet, elle l'est pour tout autre', followed by the Morita argument as on the next page.
Top-left margin note: '(i.e. les Hom sont des A-modules, et l'accouplement des Hom bilinéaire) ⟺ C préadditive, donnée un hom. d'anneaux A → End(id_C)'.
Diagonal left-margin note appears to discuss whether a) is independent of b) and c).
